en: An infamous or notorious condition or reputation.

notoriety.ety: Derived from Middle French notoriété, from Medieval Latin nōtōrietās, from nōtōrius, from nōtus (“known”), perfect passive participle of nōscō (“get to know”). By surface analysis, notorious + -ety.

note.ja: notorious（悪名高い）+ -ety。「悪評」。

en: Willing to comply with the commands, orders, or instructions of those in authority; biddable.
One who obeys.

obedient.ety: From Middle English obedient, from Old French obedient, from Latin oboediēns, present active participle of oboediō (“obey”).

ex.en: The boy is obedient to his parents.
ex.ja: その少年は両親の言うことを聞く。

ex.en: She is obedient to her parents.
ex.ja: 彼女は親の言う事を良く聞く。

ex.en: All things are obedient to money.
ex.ja: すべてのものは、お金に従順だ。

note.ja: obey（従う）+ -ent。ob + audire（聞く）。「従順な」。obedience と同じ。

en: The central boss of a volute.
An opening at the apex of a dome.

oculus.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin oculus (“eye”). Doublet of occhio.

note.ja: ラテン語 oculus（目）から。「丸窓」。ocular（目の）、binoculars（双眼鏡）と同じ。

en: Elaborately ornamented, often to excess.

ornate.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin ōrnātus, perfect passive participle of ōrnō (“to equip, adorn”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Doublet of orné.

en: To expel; to remove.

oust.ety: From Anglo-Norman ouster, oustier, from Old French oster (modern French ôter), from post-classical Latin obstare (“to remove”), classical obstāre (“to obstruct, stand in the way of”). Not related to out.

note.ja: 古フランス語 oster（取り除く）から。ラテン語 obstare（立ちはだかる）。「追い出す」。

en: Capable of being touched, felt or handled; touchable, tangible.
Obvious or easily perceived; noticeable.

To record (the testimony of a witness) which may be lost before a matter comes to trial.
Perpetual, or made perpetual; continued for an indefinite time.

en: Turned aside while against something, splitting off from a thing.
Morally wrong or evil; wicked; perverted.

ex.ja: 今の、ゼッタイなんか邪なこと考えてたでしょ。

ex.ja: 変なこと言うな！

To adorn, cover, or furnish with feathers or plumes, or as if with feathers or plumes.

Directly; suddenly; perpendicularly.
The sound of a sudden heavy fall.

ex.ja: 太ってはないよ。ちょっと、ぽっちゃりしてるだけで。

ex.ja: 正夢にならなきゃいいけど。

Something that provokes; a provocative act.

provocation.ety: From Middle English provocacioun, from Old French provocacion, from Late Latin prōvocātiō, prōvocātiōnem, from Latin prōvocō. By surface analysis, provoke + -ation. Doublet of provokatsiya.

ex.en: She lost her temper at the slightest provocation.
ex.ja: 彼女はごくささいなことでカッとなった。

The system by which cases are assigned to judges in multi-sala courts.
To award something by means of a raffle or random drawing.
To participate in a raffle.

raffle.ety: From Middle English rafle, from Old French rafle, raffle (“dice game", also "plundering”), from rafler (“to snatch, seize, carry off”), from Frankish *raffolōn, from Proto-Germanic *hrapōną, *hrēpōną (“to scratch, touch, pluck out, snatch”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kreb(h)-, *(s)kerb(h)- (“to turn, bend, shrink”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to turn, bend”). Cognate with Middle Dutch raffel (“dice game”), German raffen (“to snatch away, sweep off”), Old English hreppan (“to touch, treat, attack”).

note.ja: 古フランス語 rafle（さいころ遊び）から。「くじ引き」。

en: A starting or falling back; a rebound; a shrinking.
The state or condition of having recoiled.
To pull back, especially in disgust, horror or astonishment.
Of a firearm: to quickly push back when fired.

recoil.ety: From Old French reculer. Further from Latin re- + cūlus.

ex.en: We recoiled from the enemy's offensive.
ex.ja: われわれは敵の攻勢に後退した。

ex.en: He recoiled before his master's anger.
ex.ja: 彼は主人の怒りにひるんだ。

ex.en: Brave man as he was, he recoiled at the sight.
ex.ja: 彼は勇敢な男だったが、その光景にはたじろいだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 reculer（後ずさりする）から。re + culus（尻）。「後ずさる」→「たじろぐ・反動」。

A judge in a municipal court.

ex.ja: テープレコーダーは有用な教具です。

To cast off, repudiate.

The condition of being repentant, penitent, a state of feeling regret or remorse for having done wrong.

repentance.ety: First attested circa 14th century, from Middle English repentance, repentaunce, from Old French repentance. More at repent. By surface analysis, repent + -ance.

ex.en: Short pleasure, long repentance.
ex.ja: 喜びは短く、後悔は長し。

The Eucharist.

To expel air as if the nose were irritated.
An act of sneezing.

ex.ja: 咳やくしゃみをする時は、口元を覆いましょう。

The quality or state of not being intoxicated.

ex.en: I have a friend whose father is a veterinarian.
ex.ja: 私には、お父さんが獣医をしている友達がいる。

ex.en: I thought that Tom was a veterinarian.
ex.ja: トムって、獣医かと思ってた。

ex.en: She grew up to be a veterinarian.
ex.ja: 彼女は成長して獣医になった。

note.ja: veterinary（獣医の）+ -an。「獣医」。vet はこの短縮。

en: A place with no remaining resources; a desert.
Any barren or uninteresting place.

wasteland.ety: Inherited from Middle English wast lond, modification of earlier weste lond, from Old English weste land (“wasteland”); equivalent to waste + land.

note.ja: waste（荒れた）+ land。「荒れ地」。T. S. エリオットの詩『荒地』。

An individual or group that monitors the activities of another entity (such as an individual, corporation, non-profit group, or governmen…

To be continuously reset by a watchdog timer.

en: Resembling or characteristic of water.
Wet, soggy or soaked with water.

watery.ety: From Middle English watery, wattry, from Old English wæteriġ (“watery”), from Proto-West Germanic *watarīg. Equivalent to water + -y.

ex.en: I have watery stools.
ex.ja: 便が水のようです。

note.ja: water + -y。「水っぽい」。

To achieve by clever or devious means.
To gain something for oneself by clever or devious means.

From Middle English wesele, from Old English weosule, from Proto-West Germanic *wisulā, from Proto-Germanic *wisulǭ.
The verb is from c. 1900, from the supposed cunningness of the weasel.

ex.en: The weasel is noted for its bad smell.
ex.ja: いたちはその悪臭で知られている。

ex.en: Hey, can you stop weaseling your way in, especially at times like this?
ex.ja: ちょっと、こういう時にだけしゃしゃり出るのはやめてよ。

note.ja: 古英語 weosule から。「イタチ」→ ずるがしこい人。weasel words（逃げ口上）。

en: The outer skin of a citrus fruit, used as a flavouring or garnish.
General vibrance of flavour.
To scrape the zest from a fruit.
To make more zesty.

ex.en: Her disappearance gave zest to the mystery.
ex.ja: 彼女の失踪で謎が一段と面白くなった。

ex.en: Wit gives zest to conversation.
ex.ja: 機知は会話に趣を添える。

note.ja: フランス語 zeste（柑橘類の皮）から。皮の風味 →「熱意・妙味」。

Synonym of airplane. A game played when spoon-feeding children.

To transport by aeroplane.

Difficult or exhausting to traverse.

arduous.ety: From Latin arduus (“lofty, high, steep, hard to reach, difficult, laborious”), akin to Irish ard (“high”).

note.ja: ラテン語 arduus（険しい）から。「骨の折れる」。

To achieve a score of 6–0 (as the winner) in a tennis set.
To hold an opponent to a score of zero.

ex.ja: わぁ、たまねぎ味の、ベーグルだ。

note.ja: イディッシュ語 beygl から。ドイツ語 Bügel（輪）と同系。

en: An instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure.
Anything used as a gauge or indicator.

barometer.ety: From baro- + -meter. Coined in 1665 by Robert Boyle as a name for the instrument invented by Torricelli some 20 years earlier; soon thereafter borrowed from English into various languages.

ex.en: The barometer is falling. It's going to rain.
ex.ja: 気圧計の数値が下がっている。雨になりそうだな。

ex.en: The barometer is falling. It is going to rain.
ex.ja: 気圧計の数値が下がっている。雨になりそうだな。

ex.ja: 血圧は健康のバロメーターとして重要である。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 baros（重さ）+ metron（尺度）。「気圧計」→「指標」。

note.ja: ラテン語 boa（大蛇）から。「ボア（ヘビ）」→ ヘビのような長い襟巻き。

en: Any of various freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae.
The common carp, Cyprinus carpio.
To criticize or complain about a fault, especially for frivolous or petty reasons; to cavil.

carp.ety: From Late Middle English carpe (“the common carp (Cyprinus carpio)”), from Old French carpe, from Late Latin carpa, possibly from Proto-West Germanic *karpo (possibly due to the introduction from the fish from the Danube into England in the 14th century; whence Middle Low German karpe and Old High German charpho, karpho); further etymology unknown.

ex.en: I caught a carp in a net.
ex.ja: 私は網で鯉を捕った。

ex.en: Carp is my favorite fish.
ex.ja: 鯉は、私が一番好きな魚だよ。

ex.en: This pond is full of carp swimming around.
ex.ja: この池には鯉がうようよいる。

note.ja: 「コイ」は中世ラテン語 carpa から。「あら探しをする」は北欧語 karpa（自慢する）からで別語。

en: A hat made from the fur of the beaver.
A heavy quality of broadcloth for overcoats.

castor.ety: From Middle French castor, from Old French castor (“beaver”), from Latin castor (“beaver”), from Ancient Greek κάστωρ (kástōr), from Doric Greek κάστον (káston, “wood”).

note.ja: 「キャスター（車輪）」は caster（投げるもの）の変化形。「ビーバー（の香料）」はギリシャ語 kastōr からで別語。

en: The line that bounds a circle or other two-dimensional figure.
The length of such a line.

circumference.ety: From Latin circumferentia, from circum (“around”) + ferō (“to carry”). Displaced native Old English ymbgang.

ex.en: Is it possible to determine the diameter from the circumference?
ex.ja: 円周から直径を求めることは可能ですか？

ex.en: How do you derive the length of the circumference? I've forgotten.
ex.ja: 円周の長さの求め方ってどうでしたっけ？忘れました。

ex.en: God is an infinite sphere whose center is everywhere and circumference is nowhere.
ex.ja: 神は無限の球である。その中心は到るところにあり、その円周はどこにもない。

note.ja: circum（周りを）+ fer（運ぶ）+ ence。周りを運ぶ線 →「円周・周囲」。

en: An early manuscript book, especially one bound in the modern manner, by joining pages, as opposed to a rolled scroll.
An official list of medicines and medicinal ingredients.

codex.ety: Borrowed from Latin cōdex, variant form of caudex (“tree trunk, book, notebook”); compare caudex (in botany). Doublet of code.

note.ja: ラテン語 codex（木の幹・書字板）から。「写本」。code と同じ語源。

en: The quality of being delicate.
Something appealing, usually a pleasing food, especially a choice dish of a certain culture suggesting rarity and refinement.

delicacy.ety: From Middle English delicacie, from Middle English delicat, from Latin delicatus. Equivalent to delic(ate) + -acy.

ex.en: Is there a restaurant around here that serves local delicacies?
ex.ja: この近辺で、美味しい郷土料理を食べさせてくれるお店はありますか。

ex.en: I regard crab as a great delicacy.
ex.ja: 私はカニを大ごちそうだと思っている。

ex.en: Pufferfish is considered a delicacy in Japan.
ex.ja: フグは日本では珍味とされています。

note.ja: delicate（繊細な）+ -cy。「繊細さ」→ 繊細な味の「珍味」。

en: To make thinner by adding solvent to a solution, especially by adding water.
To weaken, especially by adding a foreign substance.
Having a low concentration.
Weak; reduced in strength by dilution; diluted.
An animal having a lighter-coloured coat than is usual.

dilute.ety: From Latin dīlūtus, from dīluere (“to wash away, dissolve, cause to melt, dilute”), from dī-, dis- (“away, apart”) + luere (“to wash”). See lave, and compare deluge.

note.ja: di（離して）+ luere（洗う）。「洗い流して薄める」。diluted と同じ。

en: The state of being dispersed.
A process of dispersing.

dispersion.ety: From disperse + -ion, from Middle English dispersioun, from Old French dispersion, from Latin dispersiō.

note.ja: disperse（散らす）+ -ion。「分散」。

en: The day when God is expected to judge the world; the end times.
Judgement day; the day of the Final Judgment; any day of decisive judgement or final dissolution.
Concerned with or predicting future universal destruction.
Given to or marked by forebodings or predictions of impending calamity.

doomsday.ety: From Middle English domes + dai, from Old English dom (“judgment”) + dæg (“day”). Equivalent to doom + -s- + day. Compare Old Norse dómsdagr (“judgement day, doomsday”).

note.ja: doom（最後の審判）+ day。「最後の審判の日」→「この世の終わり」。

en: A skill in the handling or manipulation of a situation.
The property of having elegance, grace, refinement, or skill.
To evade (a problem, situation, etc.) by using some clever argument or stratagem.
To handle or manage carefully or skilfully; to manipulate in a crafty way.

finesse.ety: From Middle English finesse (“a degree of excellence; (of metal) fineness, purity”), from Middle French finesse, Old French finesse (“a fineness; a delicacy; slenderness”), from fine, fin (“fine, thin”) (from Latin fīnis (“an end”); compare Middle English fīn (“of superior quality; precious, valuable; admirable, pleasing; pure, refined; fineness, purity; delicate, exquisite, fine; sharp, thin”)) + -esse (suffix forming nouns describing the condition of being something). The verb is derived from the noun.

note.ja: フランス語 finesse（繊細さ）から。fin（細かい）。fine と同じ。「巧妙さ」。

en: A ball of fire, especially one associated with an explosion, or (fiction, mythology) thrown as a weapon.
A feisty, strong-willed person.
To attack (someone or something) with balls of fire.
To explode in a ball of fire or flame.

fireball.ety: The noun is derived from fire (noun) + ball (noun). The adjective and verb are derived from the noun.

note.ja: fire + ball。「火の玉」。

en: A soft cloth material originally woven from wool, today often combined with cotton or synthetic fibers.
A washcloth.
Made of flannel.
To rub with a flannel.
To wrap in flannel.

flannel.ety: From Middle English flaunneol, from Anglo-Norman flanelle (compare Norman flianné), diminutive of Old French flaine, floene (“coarse wool”), from Gaulish, from Proto-Celtic *wlānos, *wlanā (“wool”) (compare Welsh gwlân, Breton gloan), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂. More at wool.

note.ja: ウェールズ語 gwlanen（毛織物）から。gwlân（羊毛）。wool と同じ祖先。

en: The main idea or substance, or the most essential part, of a longer or more complicated matter; the crux, the heart, the pith.
Gossip, rumour; (countable) an instance of this.
To extract and present the main ideas or substance, or the most essential parts of (a document, piece of writing, etc.); to abridge, to s…
To talk idly; chat; also, to gossip.

gist.ety:
The noun is derived from Old French gist, a noun use of the third person singular indicative of gesir (“to lie down”) (modern French gésir; compare Anglo-Norman (cest) action gist (literally “(law) (this) action lies”)), from Latin iacēre, the present active infinitive of iaceō (“to lie down, lie prostrate, recline”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(H)yeh₁- (“to throw”) (probably in the sense of something being thrown down).
The verb is derived from the noun.
The programming sense is a genericized trademark of GitHub Gist, introduced 2008.

ex.en: I got the gist of what he was saying.
ex.ja: 彼が言っていることの要点はわかった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 gist（〜にある・かかっている）から。法律用語 the gist of the action（訴訟の要点）から「要点」。

en: Causing grief, pain, or sorrow.
Serious, grave, dire, or dangerous.

grievous.ety: From Middle English grevous, from Anglo-Norman grevous, from Old French grever, from Latin gravō (“to burden”). Developed in the 13th century. Equivalent to grief + -ous.

note.ja: grief（悲しみ）+ -ous。ラテン語 gravis（重い）。「重大な」。grave と同じ。

en: A piece of cloth, usually square and often fine and elegant, carried for wiping the face, eyes, nose or hands.
A piece of cloth shaped like a handkerchief to be worn about the neck; a neckerchief or neckcloth.

ex.en: I got a yellow handkerchief on my birthday.
ex.ja: 誕生日に黄色のハンカチをもらいました。

ex.en: He picked up a handkerchief from the floor.
ex.ja: 彼は床からハンカチを拾った。

ex.en: How many handkerchiefs do you have there?
ex.ja: そこにハンカチが何枚ありますか？

note.ja: hand（手）+ kerchief（頭巾）。kerchief はフランス語 couvre-chef（頭を覆うもの）。「手に持つ布」。

en: The art or science of cultivating gardens; gardening.
Small-scale agriculture.

note.ja: ラテン語 hortus（庭）+ cult（耕す）+ ure。庭を耕すこと →「園芸」。

en: The protracted, mournful cry of a dog, wolf or other canid; also of other animals.
Any similar sound.
To utter a loud, protracted, mournful sound or cry, as dogs and wolves often do.
To utter a sound expressive of pain or distress; to cry aloud and mournfully; to lament; to wail.

howl.ety:
From Middle English howlen, houlen, from Old English *hūlian, from Proto-West Germanic *hūilōn, from Proto-Germanic *hūwilōną, *hiuwilōną (“to howl”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *kū-, *kew- (“to howl, scream”). Likely of imitative origin.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian huulje (“to howl”), Dutch huilen (“to cry”), Romanian a hăuli (“to howl”), Old French ouler, German Low German hulen (“to howl”), German heulen (“to howl”), Danish hyle (“to howl”), Swedish yla (“to scream, yell”), Northern Luri آلٛیر (āłir, “howl”).

ex.en: I heard the howl of a wolf.
ex.ja: オオカミの遠吠えを聞きました。

ex.en: The wolves started to howl.
ex.ja: 狼が遠吠えをしだした。

ex.en: The wolves began to howl.
ex.ja: オオカミが遠吠えをし始めた。

note.ja: 擬音語。「遠ぼえする」。howling と同じ。

impunity.ety: From Middle French impunité, from Latin impunitas, from impunis (“without punishment”).

note.ja: ラテン語 impunitas（罰がないこと）から。in + poena（罰）。「処罰されないこと」。punish と同じ。

en: The condition of being infertile; of having poor fertility.
The inability to conceive children.

infertility.ety: From Middle French infertilité, from Late Latin infertilitas.

ex.en: I got married at 30 and, at the same time, I started getting infertility treatment.
ex.ja: 30歳で結婚し、同時に不妊治療を始めました。

ex.en: Female hormone imbalance is a major cause of infertility.
ex.ja: 女性ホルモン分泌の乱れが不妊症の大きな原因です。

note.ja: in（否定）+ fertility（生殖能力）。「不妊」。

A person or organisation in an intermediate position (in a transaction, agreement, supply chain, etc.)

The large spherical tart fruit produced by this tree.

en: To call into action.
To entreat an act.

incite.ety: From Middle French inciter, from Latin incitō (“to set in motion, hasten, urge, incite”), from in (“in, on”) + citō (“to set in motion, urge”), frequentative of cieō (“to rouse, excite, call”).
